articles.title: Why is 'Mogging' the Collins' word of the year?
articles.summary: The slang word has become popular among members of Generations Z and Alpha - both online and in everyday conversation.
articles.body:
A fast-growing slang word among members of Generations Z and Alpha - both online and in everyday conversation - mogging went mainstream in 2026 with a 210% increase in its usage.

Collins' English Dictionary managing director Alex Beecroft said its lexicographers look at "how often words are used" and also "analyse patterns of usage" that reveal the latest linguistic trends.

The selection of mogging as word of the year, he said, "shows how each generation leaves its mark on language". So what does mogging mean?

The BBC's culture correspondent Noor Nanji explains.

articles.title: Quem era o jovem de Piracicaba que morreu afogado em praia de Itanhaém | G1
articles.standfirst: Maurício Gomes se afogou em trecho de praia no bairro Satélite, no domingo (1º). Ele foi enterrado nesta terça-feira (3).
articles.summary: Maurício Gomes se afogou em trecho de praia no bairro Satélite, no domingo (1º).
articles.body:
Mauricio Batista Gomes, de 24 anos, morador de Piracicaba, morreu após se afogar em praia de Itanhaém — Foto: Redes sociais

O jovem de Piracicaba (SP) que morreu afogado em uma praia de Itanhaém , no litoral de São Paulo, no último domingo (1º), foi identificado como Mauricio Batista Gomes, de 24 anos.

Mauricio se afogou em trecho de praia no bairro Satélite.

De acordo com o Grupamento de Bombeiros Marítimo (GBMar), equipes foram acionadas por uma mulher que viu um grupo de banhistas tentando salvar a vítima no mar, distante da faixa de areia.

Equipes de moto aquática e bote de salvamento inflável estiveram no local realizando buscas pelo jovem, que desapareceu nas águas. Pouco mais de uma hora depois, um banhista encontrou o corpo da vítima já na faixa de areia.

Os bombeiros realizaram manobras de RCP no jovem, que foi transportado para a UPA de Itanhaém, onde teve a morte constatada. A namorada dele reconheceu o corpo.

A vítima era formada em gestão de Recursos Humanos e tinha pós-graduação em gestão de negócios pela Escola Superior de Agricultura "Luiz de Queiroz" da Universidade de São Paulo (Esalq/USP).

Ao g1 , a namorada de Mauricio descreveu ele como uma pessoa "incrível, um menino inteligente, esperto, alegre e que tinha muitos sonhos".

Ela também destacou que o jovem amava viajar, o Flamengo e a família dele.

O velório e enterro de Mauricio aconteceram nesta terça-feira (3) no Cemitério Municipal Vila Rezende, em Piracicaba.

Segundo a namorada, Mauricio Batista Gomes amava viajar, o Flamengo e a família — Foto: Redes sociais

articles.title: PGR além do papel: como transformar riscos ocupacionais em decisões | G1
articles.standfirst: Inventário e plano de ação só geram valor quando acompanham a operação, orientam prioridades e são revistos diante de mudanças, incidentes e resultados.
articles.summary: Inventário e plano de ação só geram valor quando acompanham a operação, orientam prioridades e são revistos diante de mudanças, incidentes e resultados
articles.body:
PGR além do papel: como transformar riscos ocupacionais em decisões de gestão — Foto: Crédito: Corpmed.

Há empresas com PGR tecnicamente bem diagramado que não conseguem responder perguntas básicas: quais riscos precisam de intervenção primeiro, quem é responsável, quais medidas estão atrasadas e se os controles adotados funcionaram. Quando isso acontece, o documento existe, mas o gerenciamento não chegou à operação.

A NR-1 diferencia o Gerenciamento de Riscos Ocupacionais, o GRO, do Programa de Gerenciamento de Riscos, o PGR. O GRO é o processo de identificar perigos, avaliar e controlar riscos. O PGR materializa esse processo e deve conter, no mínimo, inventário de riscos ocupacionais e plano de ação.

As organizações abrangidas pela NR-1 devem implementar o gerenciamento de riscos por estabelecimento, observadas as dispensas e condições específicas previstas na norma para o MEI e determinados pequenos negócios. O PGR pode ser mantido em meio físico ou eletrônico, mas precisa estar atualizado, disponível e coerente com as atividades efetivamente realizadas.

O inventário reúne processos e ambientes, atividades, perigos, possíveis lesões ou agravos, grupos de trabalhadores expostos, medidas de prevenção existentes, dados de análise preliminar ou monitoramento, avaliação e classificação dos riscos e critérios utilizados. O plano de ação registra as medidas a introduzir, aprimorar ou manter, com cronograma, responsáveis e formas de acompanhamento e aferição de resultados.

Transformar essas exigências em painéis gerenciais, ritos de acompanhamento, indicadores e critérios de investimento é uma boa prática de gestão. A norma exige o processo e seus registros; não impõe um software ou modelo único de dashboard.

O inventário descreve uma realidade em determinado momento. O gerenciamento precisa acompanhar mudanças de processo, tecnologia, pessoas, organização do trabalho e eficácia das medidas.

O erro começa quando o documento é produzido à distância

Descrições genéricas de função, matrizes copiadas e planos de ação padronizados podem deixar de fora manutenção não rotineira, improvisos, picos de produção, deslocamentos, trabalho de terceiros, diferenças entre turnos e a distância entre o procedimento escrito e a atividade real.

Reconhecer o risco exige visitar ambientes, observar a atividade, consultar documentos e ouvir quem executa e supervisiona o trabalho. A participação dos trabalhadores não é apenas uma estratégia de engajamento: a NR-1 prevê mecanismos de participação e consulta, além de comunicação sobre riscos consolidados no inventário e medidas do plano de ação.

Uma lista de perigos não basta. A avaliação precisa utilizar critérios de severidade e probabilidade adequados, considerar requisitos legais, número de expostos, frequência e duração da exposição, controles existentes, dados de saúde e incidentes, além das limitações das informações disponíveis.

Classificações ajudam a comparar riscos e justificar prioridades, mas não substituem julgamento técnico. Uma matriz colorida pode criar falsa precisão quando os critérios não estão definidos ou são aplicados de modo diferente entre unidades. A empresa deve conseguir explicar por que um risco recebeu determinada classificação e como essa decisão orientou o plano.

Plano de ação precisa ter dono, prazo e evidência

Ações como ‘treinar a equipe’, ‘usar EPI’ ou ‘orientar os trabalhadores’ são insuficientes quando não indicam qual perigo será controlado, a medida selecionada, o responsável, o prazo, os recursos, a prioridade e como o resultado será verificado. Também é necessário considerar a hierarquia das medidas de prevenção, priorizando eliminação e controles coletivos antes de depender exclusivamente de medidas administrativas ou proteção individual.

A conclusão de uma tarefa não prova automaticamente sua eficácia. Instalar uma proteção, alterar uma jornada ou revisar uma meta exige verificar se a exposição foi reduzida, se surgiram riscos residuais e se a medida funciona durante a rotina, os desvios e as situações não habituais.

A avaliação de riscos é contínua. A página oficial do MTE informa revisão periódica em prazo máximo previsto pela NR-1 e revisão antecipada em situações como implantação de medidas, mudanças tecnológicas ou organizacionais, inadequação ou ineficácia dos controles, acidentes ou doenças relacionadas ao trabalho e alterações legais aplicáveis.

Na prática, novos equipamentos, mudanças de layout, aquisição de empresa, terceirização, aumento de metas, reestruturações, trabalho remoto e expansão para outro turno podem alterar o risco antes da revisão programada. Um fluxo de gestão de mudanças deve acionar SST, Saúde e Operações antes que a nova condição se torne rotina. NR-1 vigente — MTE

PCMSO, incidentes e indicadores fecham o ciclo

O PGR orienta o PCMSO ao informar riscos e grupos expostos. No sentido inverso, achados coletivos de saúde, suspeitas de exposição excessiva e doenças relacionadas ao trabalho podem exigir reavaliação do inventário e das medidas de prevenção. Essa integração deve preservar o sigilo médico e utilizar informações agregadas ou funcionais apropriadas.

Acidentes, quase acidentes, falhas operacionais, queixas e afastamentos também são sinais de aprendizagem. Eles não devem ser usados apenas para atribuir culpa. A investigação precisa reconstruir fatores técnicos e organizacionais, verificar barreiras que falharam e alimentar o inventário e o plano de ação.

Operações reconhece no inventário as atividades que realmente executa.

Trabalhadores participam da identificação, da validação e da revisão dos riscos.

Cada prioridade do plano tem responsável, prazo, recurso e indicador de acompanhamento.

Mudanças relevantes acionam avaliação antes ou logo após a implantação.

PCMSO, ergonomia, incidentes, contratadas e indicadores alimentam o mesmo ciclo de decisão.

A liderança acompanha riscos críticos e impedimentos, não apenas percentual de ações concluídas.

A empresa registra por que escolheu cada medida e verifica o risco residual.

Conformidade que conversa com a estratégia

Um PGR maduro não promete risco zero. Ele permite que a empresa conheça suas exposições, priorize recursos, demonstre critérios e aprenda com mudanças e resultados. Isso fortalece prevenção, continuidade operacional e coerência entre documentos, decisões e realidade.

A Corpmed integra PGR, PCMSO, ergonomia, riscos psicossociais, atividades críticas, indicadores e suporte às áreas de RH, Jurídico, SST e Operações. O ponto de partida varia conforme porte, processo produtivo, distribuição geográfica e maturidade da organização — porque o gerenciamento precisa ser desenhado para funcionar no contexto real de cada empresa.

O PGR DA SUA EMPRESA ACOMPANHA A OPERAÇÃO REAL?

Solicite à Corpmed um diagnóstico do PGR, da integração com o PCMSO e da capacidade do plano de ação de produzir evidências e prevenção.

Desde 2006, a Corpmed atua em saúde e segurança ocupacional com equipe multidisciplinar de mais de 30 profissionais, operação centralizada em Campinas e atendimento nacional por rede credenciada. Seu modelo integra gestão médica, SST, RH, Jurídico e Operações com suporte contínuo, rastreabilidade e uso de dados.

articles.title: Fábricas pedem banimento permanente de carros chineses nos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a agência Reuters, a associação que representa as montadoras nos EUA cobra aprovação de lei ainda neste ano e cita riscos à segurança nacional e aos investimentos.
articles.summary: Segundo a agência Reuters, a associação que representa as montadoras nos EUA cobra aprovação de lei ainda neste ano e cita riscos à segurança nacional e aos investimentos
articles.body:
Fábrica da Toyota no Texas, Estados Unidos. — Foto: Divulgação / Toyota

Uma associação que representa General Motors, Volkswagen , Toyota e outras grandes montadoras pediu ao Congresso dos Estados Unidos que aprove ainda neste ano uma proibição permanente de veículos chineses. As informações são da Reuters.

O apelo foi feito na segunda-feira (2), segundo a agência, antes da retomada dos trabalhos legislativos prevista para a próxima semana, após as eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA.

A Alliance for Automotive Innovation , que reúne quase todas as principais fabricantes, quer que os parlamentares aproveitem o curto período de votações para concluir a análise da proposta.

A entidade argumenta que a entrada desses carros ameaça tanto a segurança nacional quanto os investimentos feitos pelas montadoras no país.

Montadoras que fazem parte da Alliance for Automotive Innovation nos Estados Unidos:

Grupo Volkswagen (Audi, Lamborghini, Bentley);

“ Precisamos proteger o mercado dos Estados Unidos de uma enxurrada de importações chinesas que trazem risco de vigilância e colocam em desvantagem os fabricantes atuais que fizeram investimentos de longo alcance nas comunidades americanas”, afirmou John Bozzella, presidente da associação .

Os Estados Unidos já têm restrições que, na prática, impedem montadoras chinesas de vender ou fabricar carros de passeio no país.

A regulamentação foi adotada no início de 2025, durante o governo de Joe Biden, diante do risco de envio de dados sensíveis dos motoristas à China.

Além dessa barreira, o país mantém tarifas superiores a 100% sobre os veículos elétricos chineses . Agora, as fabricantes pressionam pela aprovação de uma lei que estabeleça o banimento permanente.

A posição do presidente Donald Trump, porém, provocou preocupação no setor.

Em setembro, Trump disse à Fox News que aceitaria que empresas chinesas produzissem carros em território americano.

Fábrica de modelos eletrificados da Leapmotor em Zhejiang, China. — Foto: Divulgação

O projeto de proibição avançou em julho, quando foi aprovado por uma comissão do Senado. Na Câmara dos Representantes, a versão da proposta já conta com mais de 100 parlamentares como coautores.

Apesar do amplo apoio, os senadores responsáveis pela iniciativa, que reúne integrantes dos dois partidos, concordaram em setembro em adiar para novembro a tentativa de acelerar a tramitação.

Montadoras e assessores legislativos ainda esperam concluir a aprovação neste ano. Mas alguns assessores do Congresso e representantes do setor avaliam que, se os democratas conquistarem o controle do Legislativo, poderá faltar tempo para votar o banimento antes do encerramento da sessão, em dezembro.

Para defender a urgência da medida, Bozzella citou o avanço dos veículos produzidos na China sobre o mercado europeu . Segundo ele, a União Europeia importou mais de 1,1 milhão de veículos do país asiático nos oito primeiros meses de 2026, volume superior ao registrado em todo o ano de 2025.

“Dado o evidente risco à segurança nacional e o padrão de comportamento desleal da China, o Congresso deve proteger nossa base de defesa e de manufatura avançada e impedir que as montadoras chinesas façam aqui o que conseguiram fazer impunemente na Europa”, declarou.

O Ministério das Relações Exteriores da China já havia pedido aos Estados Unidos que passassem “ a respeitar as leis da economia de mercado e os princípios da concorrência justa ”.

O governo chinês também classificou propostas anteriores contra empresas do país como “repressão injustificada”.

articles.title: Polícia espanhola desmonta acampamento de manifestantes em Madri | G1
articles.standfirst: Remoção de barracas de manifestantes nesta terça (3) ocorreu após ocupação de manifestantes na praça Puerta del Sol que durou 5 semanas. Organizadores do movimento denunciaram 'intervenção policial violenta'.
articles.summary: Remoção de barracas de manifestantes nesta terça (3) ocorreu após ocupação de manifestantes na praça Puerta del Sol que durou 5 semanas. Organizadores do movimento denunciaram 'intervenção policial violenta'.
articles.body:
Equipes de limpeza retiram barracas e outros objetos da praça Puerta del Sol, no centro de Madri, na Espanha, após protestos por direito à moradia, em 3 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Paul Hanna/AFP

O acampamento de ativistas pelo direito à moradia instalado há mais de cinco semanas em uma praça no centro de Madri foi desmantelado na madrugada desta terça-feira (3), anunciaram as autoridades e os organizadores do movimento.

"A retirada do acampamento da (praça) Porta do Sol aconteceu sem distúrbios, nem episódios de violência", informaram fontes da delegação do governo de Madri . No total, 334 pessoas foram retiradas e duas foram detidas por desobediência e resistência.

Os organizadores do movimento denunciaram no Telegram "uma intervenção policial violenta" que deixou "várias companheiras feridas em consequência dos golpes e do uso de gás de pimenta".

"O dispositivo foi integrado por 220 agentes da Polícia Nacional e 180 da Polícia Municipal de Madri , com a participação de bombeiros e serviços sociais", afirmou a delegação do governo, que celebrou uma "operação que permitiu concluir a retirada sem alterações violentas da ordem pública".

Na manhã de terça-feira, grande parte da praça foi fechada pelas forças de segurança e operações de limpeza estavam em curso.

A crise de moradia, uma das maiores preocupações dos espanhóis, voltou ao debate público no fim de setembro após a expulsão de sua residência de Maricarmen Abascal, uma aposentada madrilena de 87 anos que morreu poucos dias depois.

A expulsão da idosa de seu apartamento desencadeou uma onda de manifestações e protestos, como a instalação do acampamento de protesto na praça Porta do Sol.

Incapaz de obter a aprovação no Parlamento de dois projetos de lei destinados a enfrentar o problema, o primeiro-ministro Pedro Sánchez convocou eleições legislativas antecipadas para 29 de novembro.

DURANTE O PROTESTO: Manifestantes em barracas na praça Puerta del Sol em Madri, na Espanha, protestam contra despejo de idosa de 87 anos em 28 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Juan Medina

articles.title: Cão farejador acha 76 kg de cocaína em peças em Campo Grande | G1
articles.standfirst: Droga saiu de Ponta Porã com destino a Curitiba e foi descoberta em uma transportadora de Campo Grande, durante ação da Receita Federal.
articles.summary: Apreensão de cocaína em Campo Grande: cão farejador localiza 76 kg da droga ocultos em peças de máquinas agrícolas que seriam enviadas de Mato Grosso do Sul para Curitiba.
articles.body:
A Receita Federal apreendeu 76 quilos de cocaína escondidos em peças de máquinas agrícolas em uma transportadora de Campo Grande . A droga saiu de Ponta Porã (MS) e tinha como destino Curitiba (PR). A apreensão contou com a ajuda de um cão farejador.

Segundo a Receita Federal, a droga foi encontrada durante uma ação de inteligência que monitora o transporte de encomendas em Mato Grosso do Sul. O trabalho inclui a análise de notas fiscais e outros documentos para identificar cargas suspeitas.

A cocaína estava escondida em peças de máquinas agrícolas e foi localizada após a encomenda chegar à transportadora na capital sul-mato-grossense.

Droga encontrada no local — Foto: Receita Federal

Ninguém foi preso durante a apreensão. A Receita Federal informou que a transportadora também é considerada vítima e, por isso, não terá o nome divulgado.

O caso será investigado pela polícia, que deverá identificar quem enviou a encomenda e os responsáveis pelo tráfico da droga.

articles.standfirst: Caso aconteceu na altura do bairro Santa Rita.
articles.summary: Caso aconteceu na altura do bairro Santa Rita.
articles.body:
Acidente deixa feridos na BR-393, em Barra Mansa — Foto: Divulgação/Redes sociais

Um acidente envolvendo dois carros deixou duas pessoas gravemente feridas na manhã desta terça-feira (3), na BR-393, em Barra Mansa (RJ). O caso aconteceu na altura do bairro Santa Rita.

Equipes do Corpo de Bombeiros estão no local prestando atendimento as vítimas. De acordo com o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (SAMU), duas vítimas sofreram ferimentos graves e foram encaminhadas para um hospital da região, ainda não divulgado.

O g1 entrou em contato com as autoridades para apurar as circunstâncias do ocorrido.

articles.title: Revisão preparatória para o Enem acontece nesta quarta em Teresina  | G1
articles.standfirst: O Pré-Enem Seduc Day reunirá estudantes para uma revisão intensiva de todas as disciplinas do Enem, das 8h às 17h30, no Theresina Hall, em Teresina.
articles.summary: O Pré-Enem Seduc Day promove revisão intensiva no Theresina Hall e anuncia o Passe Livre Enem 2026 para garantir o deslocamento dos estudantes da rede pública.
articles.body:
O Pré-Enem Seduc Day será realizado nesta quarta-feira (4), das 8h às 17h30, no Theresina Hall, em Teresina , e deve reunir cerca de 3,8 mil estudantes da rede pública. O evento contará com revisão intensiva para o Enem e todas as disciplinas cobradas no exame, além de foco nos conteúdos e habilidades exigidos pelo exame.

A iniciativa é promovida pela Secretaria de Estado da Educação do Piauí (Seduc), em parceria com o Ministério da Educação (MEC). Segundo a secretaria, o evento vai reunir estudantes da 3ª série do Ensino Médio da rede pública estadual e alunos do Instituto Federal do Piauí (IFPI).

Além das revisões, o evento terá espaços com dinâmicas interativas para incentivar a participação dos estudantes. A programação também inclui um espaço dedicado à um podcast, com conversas e produção de conteúdos sobre educação.

Segundo a Seduc, durante o evento será anunciado o Passe Livre Enem 2026 , voltado para estudantes da capital e do interior do estado que tem como objetivo facilitar o deslocamento dos participantes até os locais de prova e ampliar o acesso ao exame.

articles.title: Australia’s High Court hears bid to overturn under-16s social media ban
articles.summary: Online giant Reddit and advocacy group Digital Freedom Project argue ban is unconstitutional.
articles.body:
Australia’s world-first social media ban for under-16s faces its first major legal test in the High Court, almost one year after taking effect.

The challenge was brought on Tuesday by online platform Reddit and Australian advocacy group Digital Freedom Project.

Reddit has highlighted a number of issues in its written submission to the court, pointing to problems enforcing the ban and a lack of scientific evidence about the harms of social media.

“The evidence so far is that the effectiveness of the ban has been limited,” Reddit’s submission reads.

Social media companies were forced to delete millions of accounts after Australia banned those aged below 16 from the likes of Facebook, TikTok, YouTube and Reddit last December.

The platforms are responsible for identifying and deleting the accounts of underage users, and face hefty fines if they are found in breach of their obligations.

Reddit argued this approach was actually more dangerous, as registered accounts were governed by in-built safety features.

Material posted on many online platforms and social media sites could still be accessed without an account, Reddit said.

“Young people using other platforms without an account are also unable to be protected from exposure to particular harmful content as they previously had been,” its submission read.

Australia said its restrictions would protect young users from graphic content and online predators.

While there is a growing body of evidence about the harms of social media, Reddit argued there was no “scientific consensus”.

A team of Australia-based researchers published a study in August that found little evidence to suggest teenagers have stopped using social media despite the ban.

Digital Freedom Project, led by New South Wales politician John Ruddick, believes the ban is unconstitutional because it restricts teenagers’ ability to take part in political discourse.

“Social media is an important means of accessing news and engaging in political communication for young Australians, including children under 16,” the advocacy group argued in written submissions.

“The restriction also risks removing beneficial sources of connection, support and participation,” it added.

Digital Freedom Project, according to its website, comprises a group of Australians who are concerned about increasing government intervention and censorship in the digital space.

Reddit and the Digital Freedom Project separately announced last year they would challenge the ban.

It was unclear how long the court would take to consider the case.

The Australian government has stepped up online and social media restrictions to protect young people from pressures and risks they could be exposed to while logged in to social media accounts, according to the online regulator, eSafety Commissioner.

The government has also proposed opt-out laws which would force social media companies to give users the choice to turn off their algorithm.

Meta and its social media platforms Facebook and Instagram are facing a class action lawsuit in Australia over allegations that addictive design features are harming children and teenagers.

The class action suit was filed on behalf of eight plaintiffs who allege they were harmed by Meta while they were below the age of 18.

articles.title: PFAS: Major study into 'forever chemicals' in UK population
articles.summary: The government is launching the first study to measure PFAS in the UK population to understand the risks.
articles.body:
The government is launching its first study into the levels of so-called 'forever chemicals' in the UK population.

By taking blood and urine samples, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) hopes to gain a better understanding of any potential health risks caused by the substances also known as PFAS, as well as other potential contaminants like lead and arsenic.

It said current evidence suggested the possible health impacts associated with PFAS are likely to be limited, but said the strongest links found in large population groups have been to raised cholesterol and lower birth weights.

The first results are expected next year.

PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances) have been used prolifically since the 1940s and 1950s because they are resistant to water, oil and heat.

It is why they have been placed in thousands of items such as pots and pans, clothing and foams used to fight fires.

But because they do not break down easily in the environment - hence the name 'forever chemicals' - they have raised health concerns in recent years.

Two are already banned in the UK - PFOA and PFOS - because prolonged exposure to them can increase the risk of cancer, according to the World Health Organization.

But the study of PFAS is an emerging field with more than 15,000 types to research.

The UKHSA will take blood and urine samples collected through the existing Health Survey for England to establish baseline levels of PFAS, lead, arsenic, bisphenols, phthalates and flame retardants in the population.

In an exclusive interview with BBC Radio 4's Inside Health, Dr Edward Wynne-Evans, director of radiation, chemicals, climate and environmental hazards at the UKHSA, said there are gaps around "what different levels of exposure mean for an individual's long-term health".

There are growing concerns among people living near sites where there has been contamination from the two known toxic PFAS, and they have chosen to get individual blood tests.

In September, blood tests found "really high levels" of one of the cancer-causing forever chemicals (PFOA) in dozens of people living near a major chemical factory.

But the UK government does not recommend individuals get routine PFAS blood testing because there is no "established clinical intervention" if they have elevated levels, Wynne-Evans said.

"If you are going to do a test where you cannot recommend an action to follow, we would not normally recommend a test."

He said that this study would help "build an evidence base to better understand what might be happening".

Speaking before this study was announced, Prof Tony Fletcher from the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine said he believed there is a low level of PFAS in everyone's blood.

"If we tested a random sample of anybody's blood, we would measure [PFAS] in low levels."

"We are not all dying because of this but at higher levels [and in larger populations] they have been associated with adverse health effects."

For the two banned PFAS - PFOA and PFOS - the known risks include increased cholesterol, an increased risk of cancer, reduced antibody levels following childhood vaccinations and a range of endocrine effects linked to the thyroid and lower birth weights.

"I have met with people living in an area with contamination - they are angry," Fletcher said.

"What I try and explain to them is we have found these causal associations between exposure and effect in studying large populations. Although at an individual level, the chances of you getting some bad disease or some adverse health effect is quite low."

He stated the important thing is to stop ongoing exposure, to avoid any long-term effects.

Inside Health was produced by Imogen Harper and Tom Bonnett. And additional reporting by Esme Stallard.

articles.title: When will we know the US midterm election results?
articles.summary: The first results are expected on Tuesday as polls begin to close at 23:00 GMT. But final results might take days.
articles.body:
On Tuesday night, the United States – and many people around the world – will be following one of the country’s most closely contested midterm elections in recent years.

All 435 seats in the US House of Representatives and 35 of the 100 Senate seats are up for grabs as Democrats hope to take control of both chambers from President Donald Trump’s Republican Party.

The first results should be known on Tuesday, after polls begin to close, and will be shown on Al Jazeera’s live results page . Voting will end first in some jurisdictions on the East Coast at 6pm (23:00 GMT).

Results will continue to come in throughout Tuesday evening, and some probably won’t be known until Wednesday or later in some races as more states finish voting and officials start releasing their vote counts.

But the first reported results will not necessarily mean that a winner has been announced.

Election officials release vote counts as ballots are processed, and news organisations, such as The Associated Press, analyse them to determine how to call a race.

A closely contested race could take hours to call – or even days. It might not be clear for days whether the Republicans will retain control of Congress or Democrats secure a majority in either or both chambers.

The first polling stations to close will be in parts of Indiana and Kentucky.

6pm Eastern Standard Time (EST) (23:00 GMT) – parts of Indiana and Kentucky

7pm EST (00:00 GMT) – most of Florida, Georgia, South Carolina, Vermont, Virginia, and the remaining parts of Indiana, Kentucky and most of New Hampshire

7:30pm EST (00:30 GMT on Wednesday) – North Carolina, Ohio, West Virginia

8pm EST (01:00 GMT on Wednesday) – Alabama, Connecticut, Delaware, Illinois, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Mississippi, Missouri, the remaining parts of New Hampshire, New Jersey, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Washington, DC, and parts of Florida, Kansas, Michigan, North Dakota, South Dakota and Texas

8:30pm EST (01:30 GMT on Wednesday ) – Arkansas

9pm EST (02:00 GMT on Wednesday) – Arizona, Colorado, Iowa, Louisiana, Minnesota, Nebraska, New Mexico, New York, Wisconsin, Wyoming, and the remaining parts of Kansas, Michigan, North Dakota, South Dakota and Texas

10pm EST (03:00 GMT on Wednesday) – Montana, Nevada, Utah, and parts of Idaho and Oregon

11pm EST (04:00 GMT on Wednesday) – California and Washington, and the remaining parts of Idaho and Oregon

12am EST (05:00 GMT on Wednesday) – Hawaii and most of Alaska

1am EST (06:00 GMT on Wednesday) – the remaining parts of Alaska, including the western Aleutian Islands

Which states could take longer to count votes?

Alaska : The state uses ranked-choice voting. If no candidate receives more than 50 percent of the vote, extra rounds of counting are needed to determine the winner. And while in-person early and Election Day voting are reported on election night, the mail-in voting results are released in the following days. In 2024, about 75 percent of the votes were counted by the morning after the election with the remaining votes reported over the following days.

California: The state carries out elections primarily by mail. Large batches of ballots come in and are verified days after the polls close, so close House races can take days or weeks to resolve.

Arizona: In some counties, voters drop off mail-in ballots on Election Day. These ballots must undergo signature checks before being counted, which can delay results by several days in close races.

Nevada: All registered voters are mailed ballots. Mail-in ballots postmarked by Election Day can arrive up to four days later. Voters also have six days after Election Day to fix any signature problem, and this could delay results until the following week.

Maine: Like Alaska, this state also uses ranked-choice voting. If no candidate receives more than 50 percent of the vote in a race with two candidates, ballots must be taken to Augusta, Maine’s capital, for further counting. This can delay final results.

Washington: The state holds elections by mail. Ballots postmarked by Election Day can be counted in the following days, which can cause delays.

Which states could report results earlier?

Some of the states that could report results earlier include:

Florida: Votes are usually counted quickly. In the 2024 general election, about 99 percent of the votes were counted by 10:51pm EST (03:51 GMT the next day), according to The Associated Press news agency.

Ohio: Ohio tends to release all or almost all of its early and absentee voting results in the first results. The first results of the 2024 elections were reported starting at 7:36pm EST (00:36 GMT), six minutes after polls closed. By 11:03pm EST (04:03 GMT), 90 percent of the results had been reported.

North Carolina: This East Coast state is also expected to release most of its results from mail-in voting in the first update of the night. In 2024, the state reached 90 percent of vote reporting at 11:36pm EST (04:36 GMT).

Pennsylvania: In 2024, the first results came in as polls closed at 8pm EST (01:00 GMT). Half of the votes had been reported by 10:12pm EST (03:12 GMT), rising to 90 percent by 12:48am EST (05:48 GMT) the next day.

Wisconsin: In 2024, 90 percent of the state voting results were released by 2:22am (07:22 GMT) on November 6.

Many races could be called on election night, but it might take several days to know which party will control the House and Senate in the final two years of Trump’s presidency.

If, for example, the US Senate race in Alaska requires a ranked-choice tabulation, the next round is scheduled for November 18.

So there is no specific deadline for knowing all the results. In races that are not close, news organisations are able to declare winners well before every ballot is counted while official certification takes place later. So quick reporting does not guarantee a fast race call.

In 2024, it took eight days to determine which party would control the House of Representatives.

If a race is very close, a recount might be triggered automatically or if requested by a candidate, depending on state law.

Candidates also have the option of challenging the results in court, which could also delay the final result.

Trump has also raised questions about whether he would accept the midterm election results. When he was asked if he would respect the final outcome, he said: “I will if there are honest elections.”

But the US president cannot overturn congressional election results simply because he disagrees with them. Elections are administered and certified by individual states, and legal challenges must follow a process.

“All the states run elections. Courts accept that states run elections,” Democratic strategist Mali Smith told Al Jazeera.

Under the US Constitution , the House and Senate have the final authority to judge disputes over the elections of their own members.

Depending on the dispute, recounts and legal challenges could take days, weeks or longer to resolve.

articles.title: 'We're out of time': Florida pilot's desperate final warning before private jet plunged to ground, killing 9
articles.summary: The pilot of the Florida Learjet 60 crash sent out increasingly desperate distress calls moments before the aircraft plunged into a Florida roadway on
articles.body: The pilot of the Florida Learjet 60 crash sent out increasingly desperate distress calls moments before the aircraft plunged into a Florida roadway on Sunday, killing all nine people on board. In a chilling final exchange with air traffic controllers, the pilot warned that the aircraft was descending at an extreme speed and cried out, “We’re going to crash into the ground!” CNN reported, citing air traffic control recordings.The aircraft was travelling from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas when it crashed in Palm Beach County, Florida. Its final radio transmissions captured the crew's desperate attempts to communicate the unfolding emergency.According to the report, the pilot had reported ice accumulating on the aircraft, an outside air temperature of -47 degrees Celsius and moderate turbulence shortly before the plane began its rapid descent.‘Mayday, mayday’: Pilot reports emergencyThe distress calls began at around 12.48 pm ET, when the aircraft was flying over Palm Beach County.According to recordings of air traffic control communications captured by LiveATC.net, the pilot initially reported precipitation and requested permission to climb to 37,000 feet. Air traffic control approved the request.However, seconds later, the pilot declared, “Mayday, mayday!”The aircraft had begun descending rapidly. The pilot first reported a descent rate of 8,000 feet per minute, which soon increased to 10,000 feet per minute.‘We're descending 10,000 feet per minute’As the situation deteriorated, the pilot informed the Miami Air Route Traffic Control Center about the aircraft's rapidly increasing descent rate.“We’re descending 10,000 feet per minute!” Filgueiras told the control centre.Moments later, the warning became more urgent.“We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute,” she yelled. “We’re going to crash into the ground!”At 12.49 pm, the pilot reported that the aircraft was falling at 22,000 feet per minute, equivalent to around 367 feet per second.The final transmission came at 12.49.17 pm.“We’re out of time.”Flight-tracking data from ADS-B Exchange showed that the aircraft had plunged around 27,000 feet in approximately one minute before its signal was lost.What happened before the aircraft lost control?CNN reported that the pilot had described icing conditions and moderate turbulence shortly before the emergency.The aircraft was flying at approximately 35,000 feet, where temperatures can be extremely low. The pilot reported an outside air temperature of -47 degrees Celsius and described “light, clear ice that is manageable and moderate turbulence”.The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) said weather conditions were a major focus of its investigation.Icing is a serious aviation hazard. According to the Federal Aviation Administration, ice accumulation can increase an aircraft's weight, reduce lift, decrease thrust and increase drag. It can also make controlling the aircraft's speed and flight path more difficult.The NTSB said investigators were also examining evidence that the aircraft may have broken apart before hitting the ground.The cause of the crash remains under investigation. articles.title: Welsh public sector unlikely to meet net zero carbon plans, say auditors
articles.summary: A watchdog has criticised the lack of progress made by organisations in tackling climate change.
articles.body:
A spending watchdog has strongly criticised the lack of progress made by public sector organisations in tackling climate change.

Audit Wales says since a Welsh government "climate emergency" was declared in 2019, "decarbonisation" has become a lower priority for public bodies.

It says there are many examples of positive changes but the "collective ambition" for a net zero public sector in Wales by 2030 is unlikely to be met.

It has been estimated that it would cost at least £2.3bn to decarbonise Welsh council buildings alone.

The Welsh government said its 2030 ambition had "driven action and leadership, but it's clear that there is more work to do".

Net zero means balancing the amount of planet-warming "greenhouse" gases produced by human activities with the amount being actively removed from the atmosphere.

Effectively this means no longer adding to the total amount of these gases in the atmosphere to limit climate change.

Wales facing unrecognisable future, warns commissioner

In its new report, the spending watchdog said public bodies in all sectors recognise decarbonisation is important.

But it said: "Since 2022, financial and political pressures have caused decarbonisation to fall down the priority list.

"Public bodies told us their overall financial pressures mean they are struggling to invest in decarbonisation."

It criticised the Welsh government for not defining the "collective ambition" for net zero by 2030 as a "target".

"There are also no penalties or incentives to drive compliance. Some public bodies told us this had added to uncertainty around the level of priority to attach to carbon reduction."

On spending, it added that public bodies had made "limited progress" overall in understanding how much it will cost to decarbonise in the near or longer term.

"Where public bodies have estimated the longer-term cost, some described it as unaffordable."

Ann-Marie Harkin from Audit Wales said: "We can list positive examples, but not enough progress has been made overall, and we owe it to future generations to do better."

In 2017, the then-Labour Welsh government called for a net zero public sector by 2030, saying that public bodies were "uniquely placed" to influence emissions in areas such as buildings and transport.

The thinking was that if government-backed bodies made the switch and invested in infrastructure like electric vehicles and charge points, renewable power and heating systems, it would make it easier and cheaper for the public to follow suit.

The "collective ambition" does not require every public body to reach net zero individually by 2030 but it is meant to provide a shared direction of travel and an expectation that all public bodies contribute towards reducing emissions.

Responding to the report, a spokesperson for the Welsh government said: "A net zero public sector is a priority for Welsh government.

"We want to continue to support the decarbonisation of the public sector to lower emissions, energy bills and strengthen energy security.

"The 2030 ambition has driven action and leadership, but it's clear that there is more work to do on decarbonisation across and beyond the public sector in Wales."

The current Plaid Cymru government's ambition is for Wales, as a whole, to reach net zero by 2040 - which is ten years sooner than the current legally binding target for Wales and UK.

articles.title: Sudan’s displaced return to new challenges in war-battered Khartoum
articles.summary: The capital was one of the first areas to be affected, and one of the worst hit, by the war between the SAF and the RSF.
articles.body:
Khartoum, Sudan – Mohamed Mahdi Makki Farah, 51, returned home near the Sudanese capital in August 2025 after the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) declared the entire state of Khartoum free of Rapid Support Forces (RSF) fighters. But it was not the end of his family’s struggles.

The 51-year-old had left his home in Jabal Awliya, south of Khartoum, for el-Fasher in North Darfur in June 2023.

He returned home to find it destroyed and ransacked, with even the household utensils stolen.

“Everything had been completely destroyed. Now we sleep on the floor, and some of us are living in rented houses,” Makki Farah told Al Jazeera. “We have not made any decision to repair our home because the costs are extremely high, and we have not been able to start.”

His years as a trader appeared to have been wasted, with his possessions gone and his business capital reduced to almost a third of its pre-war level because of the Sudanese pound’s depreciation.

The journey of displacement and return exhausted his remaining resources, while children’s medical expenses and the family’s daily needs added to their financial burden.

This meant he was unable to generate the funds needed to repair his home, so rent became an additional burden, while access to water, electricity and healthcare services is still difficult.

They had also lost important documents during the war and had to start from scratch to replace them.

“Everyone knows about the water and electricity problems; Khartoum is almost entirely in darkness now. As for healthcare, only government health centres are operating, thank God,” Makki Farah said.

The family’s experiences are those faced by millions of Sudanese families returning to their homes after years of displacement.

Fighting between the SAF and the RSF, which began in April 2023, continues, particularly in the southeast of the country. But large parts of Sudan are more stable after government victories, particularly around Khartoum. Sudanese displaced from these areas during early years of fighting are beginning to return home now that the situation has improved.

According to the International Organization for Migration’s (IOM) Displacement Tracking Matrix report, as of September 30, approximately 5.27 million displaced Sudanese returned to their homes in nine states.

Of those, 82 percent had been internally displaced, while 18 percent had crossed the borders. Children accounted for about half of all returnees.

According to an assessment published by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in August 2026, approximately 2.5 million people had returned to their homes in Khartoum state.

But the agency warned that returning did not necessarily mean people had the conditions needed to rebuild their lives. Many found their homes damaged or uninhabitable, while work opportunities remained limited. Access to water and basic services was also inadequate due to damage to infrastructure during the war.

Many returnees are still renting as they cannot afford to repair their homes.

Abubakr Ishaq Hamed Ibrahim, 40, returned to Khartoum in February 2026 after being displaced to River Nile state in May 2023.

Like Makki Farah, he also found his home destroyed, with the furniture, bedding and basic household belongings they had accumulated over the years gone.

They had to move to Omdurman, neighbouring Khartoum, renting a home in the al-Thawra neighbourhood, but this became difficult to afford without a regular income.

“Our homes were looted and destroyed. We found nothing inside. Everything was wrecked, and we had no furniture, no bedding, nothing at all. We were unable to pay the rent for several months, and rents are quite expensive. We have been through extremely difficult conditions, and even now we have no stable source of income,” he said.

Before the war, Hamed Ibrahim had relied on self-employed work, but now depends on any casual work he can find.

His family had exhausted all their savings and borrowed money from family and friends to cover basics such as food, housing and school fees.

“Thank God, we are now doing casual jobs. The income is not enough to meet the cost of living and the daily burdens. We have exhausted all the money and savings we had, and we have borrowed money from individuals,” he said.

Things are slightly improving. His children have returned to school with support from relatives.

The family also receives in-kind assistance from organisations such as the World Food Programme, including supplies of sorghum (a cereal grain), flour, wheat, oil and sugar.

But overall, the situation in Khartoum remains dire for most residents. There have been fuel shortages and repeated power cuts in recent weeks, disrupting public transport. Fares have increased on some routes and commuters are often forced to wait hours for a bus. There are also long queues outside bakeries in some areas due to shortages of flour.

Families with limited resources, few employment opportunities and homes in need of costly repairs have been the worst affected.

On Saturday, Khartoum state authorities announced measures to address the transport crisis. Governor Ahmed Osman Hamza chaired a meeting that agreed to supply public transport services with fuel and give buses priority.

Government departments were also instructed to give residents lifts when travelling to and from work. Members of the Popular Resistance of Sudan, a coalition of SAF-aligned armed factions, help manage traffic in the capital.

Economic journalist and specialist Khalid Takes said the public transport crisis in Khartoum highlights a need for the state to take more responsibility for managing a centralised process, away from a reliance on private minibuses.

“No country has left the public transport sector entirely in the hands of the private sector, which relies on small vehicles,” he told Al Jazeera. “This results in ongoing costs for the state, both directly and indirectly, particularly in importing spare parts and fuel, which require foreign currency.”

Makki Farah says although he has managed to return to his home city of Khartoum, it is not enough to return his life to how it was before the war. He does not see a future in the capital for his family unless they receive more support.

“We have lost everything we had before the war. Now we need assistance because everything we need – housing, healthcare and education – has been destroyed,” he said.

articles.title: Whitby museum and art gallery repair bill could hit £200k
articles.summary: A council report says major investment is needed in the Whitby building.
articles.body:
Whitby Museum and Pannett Art Gallery could require £200,000 of repair work to address concerns about the condition of the historic building.

The figure represents a huge increase on the current £18,000 which has been allocated by the town council for general repairs and maintenance of the building.

A report to councillors said that "substantial investment" was required and confirmed a series of specialist surveys had been commissioned to identify the scale of the work required.

The findings will be used to inform future investment decisions and help determine the full long-term cost of maintaining the building.

The specialist surveys will include a full building condition survey, asbestos surveys, measured building surveys, and specialist mechanical and electrical assessments.

According to the Local Democracy Reporting Service , council papers showed the museum and art gallery brought in £96,911 during the year, but it cost £154,685 to run.

Because its costs were higher than its income, the council had to provide funding to help cover the shortfall, the papers stated.

They also indicate that borrowing may be required to fund future works.

Councillors were set to discuss the museum and art gallery's proposed budget and future investment requirements at a meeting that was scheduled to be held this week but has since been cancelled.

articles.title: Drivers may get compensation offers before car finance saga ends
articles.summary: The regulator says it supports lenders offering early compensation offers, as long as they are fair.
articles.body:
Drivers may be offered compensation from lenders ahead of the next legal battle in the car finance mis-selling saga.

Regulator the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) said it would welcome lenders making settlement offers as long as customers were not given a worse deal than under its proposed central scheme.

That scheme is facing a legal challenge, to be heard in February, with resulting compensation unlikely to be paid until late next year.

But Barclays has confirmed it will make early compensation offers from now, with others expected to follow suit.

The FCA said it would still only expect a minority of claimants to be made early offers, with most having to wait for the outcome of next year's court case.

Stephen Braviner Roman, the FCA's general counsel and co-lead on the motor finance project, said: "Fair settlement offers could result in some people getting money sooner. It's clear they want the choice.

"Anyone who wants to wait can, and there's no obligation to agree to the offer. We'll closely monitor firms making offers and expect them to be clear what accepting an offer means."

The vast majority of new cars, and many second-hand ones, are bought with finance agreements. Customers pay an initial deposit to secure the vehicle, then a monthly fee with interest.

But millions of drivers who took out a car loan between April 2007 and November 2024 will be entitled to compensation after the loans were mis-sold.

They mostly related to when car dealers received commission from lenders, based on the interest rate charged to the customer. These were known as discretionary commission arrangements (DCAs) and customers were often not told about them.

Average compensation payouts of about £829 are expected to be made related to about 12 million car loans - about 37% of the total number during the period.

Car finance compensation payments delayed until next year

Compensation will cost the industry up to £9.1bn, including administrative costs. Individual payouts will vary, depending on the degree of harm each driver faced.

With huge compensation payouts inevitable, some lenders have already set aside millions of pounds to cover the cost.

Barclays has decided to start making compensation payments early, potentially to start clearing the cost off its balance sheet. It pointed out that claimants had already faced "a considerable wait".

"By making these early settlement offers, we are giving some customers the option of receiving redress sooner, rather than waiting for the legal challenges and any subsequent FCA action to conclude," said a Barclays Partner Finance spokesperson.

"Each offer will be calculated using the FCA's redress scheme methodology. We will clearly explain how it has been calculated and what accepting a full and final settlement means, so customers can decide whether accepting the offer is right for them."

The lender said claimants would start to be contacted directly "in the coming weeks".

But it stressed not all customers whose complaints were acknowledged on or before 1 October 2026 would receive an early settlement offer.

Guidelines on whether to accept an offer

The FCA has published a factsheet to help drivers work out whether they should accept early settlements from lenders.

It will include a list of lenders who are making early offers, to ensure claimants with other lenders are not scammed.

The regulator said lenders will need to be clear with people about what accepting any offer means. This includes:

Being able to keep any payment, even if the final settlement under the central scheme after the legal challenges proved to be smaller

Claimants would not be able to claim more later if the outcome of the legal challenge meant they would have been paid more

Accepting an offer takes you out of the scheme and stops any further input from the financial ombudsman

The Finance and Leasing Association, which represents lenders, said: "We want to see consumers receive the fairest outcome in as timely a way as possible and recognise that, in some cases, that may point to early settlement, while in others it may be appropriate to await greater legal certainty."

But Kevin Durkin, solicitor advocate and director at HD Law, who represented Marcus Johnson who won his case in the Supreme Court, said he had "real reservations" that fair compensation would be offered.

"These are only heightened by reports that just a small number of claimants will receive what could be lowball offers. I fear this is crumbs from the table, for some customers who are highly likely to be owed more, while the vast majority will receive no offer at all," he said.

The main proposed FCA scheme remains partially suspended, pending legal challenges in February.

Consumer group Consumer Voice said the proposed compensation scheme left "too many people short-changed". Three lenders - Volkswagen Financial Services, Mercedes Benz Financial Services, and Credit Agricole Auto Finance - are also challenging the scheme.

The UK's Upper Tribunal has agreed to hear legal challenges to the scheme, with a hearing scheduled from 16 February to 3 March.

Anyone who is concerned about their car finance deal and has not yet complained can still complain directly to their lender. There is information on the FCA website on how to complain for free .

articles.title: Spanish soccer player Jesus de Miguel dies after collision in match
articles.summary: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel died Tuesday at the age of 30, a day after suffering a cardiac arrest following a collision during a match, the Spanish second-tier club said.
articles.body: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel died Tuesday at the age of 30, a day after suffering a cardiac arrest following a collision during a match, the Spanish second-tier club said. “Racked with pain, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic passing of Jesus de Miguel Alameda,” the club said. “There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness.” The match against FC Andorra was abandoned seven minutes into stoppage time after De Miguel collapsed following a collision with away goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who had rushed out of his area to clear a long ball and struck the striker in the chest with his knee. De Miguel lay motionless as players from both teams desperately signaled for medical assistance. Owono was shown a straight red card. Medical staff treated the player on the pitch for more than five minutes before he was taken to the hospital by ambulance. The Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) postponed all matches scheduled for Tuesday, including fixtures in the Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina. The governing body also called off the official presentation for Spain’s Under-21 international against Japan as a mark of respect and solidarity towards De Miguel’s family, teammates and Tenerife supporters. UEFA announced that a period of silence would be observed before all European games this week. Spanish sides Atletico Madrid, Barcelona and Villarreal are in Champions League action on Tuesday. “We are heartbroken by the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda,” UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin said. “We have searched for words and found only silence.” Football clubs across Spain paid tributes to De Miguel. “Our thoughts and support are with his family, friends and loved ones during these difficult times,” Barcelona said in a statement. “Real Madrid wishes to express its condolences and affection to his family, his teammates, his club, and all his loved ones,“ the club said. De Miguel was born in Madrid in 1996 and joined Tenerife from Castellon ahead of the 2025-26 campaign, scoring 11 goals last season.

articles.title: Laser weapons add another layer of security at Trump's Mar-a-Lago estate amid rising drone threats
articles.summary: The US has deployed a laser-based anti-drone weapon at President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida, strengthening security against potential
articles.body: The US has deployed a laser-based anti-drone weapon at President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida, strengthening security against potential aerial threats.According to a report by The War Zone (TWZ), at least one AeroVironment LOCUST laser system, mounted on a 4×4 Joint Light Tactical Vehicle (JLTV), was spotted at the estate in photographs taken by photographer Andrew Harnik on October 31.The deployment adds another layer to the existing air-defence network around Mar-a-Lago, which includes Avenger short-range air-defence systems armed with Stinger missiles, radar and electronic warfare equipment.The broader security network also includes elements of the military's Counter-Unmanned Aircraft System (C-UAS) Fly-Away Kits, equipped with Ku-band radar, electronic support measures (ESM), jammers and 360-degree infrared search-and-track systems. These systems help detect, track and counter potential drone incursions around the estate, according to TWZ.Confirming the deployment, NORAD and US northern command told TWZ that the systems were deployed at the request of the US Secret Service. "These assets add a complementary layer of technology to enhance protection," the commands said.How the LOCUST laser weapon can take down dronesDeveloped by US defence manufacturer AeroVironment, LOCUST X3 is a third-generation high-energy directed-energy weapon designed to counter unmanned aerial systems (UAS).According to the manufacturer's official specifications, the system operates in the 20–35-plus kilowatt power class and is designed to defeat Group 1 to Group 3 drones, including small and tactical unmanned aircraft.The system uses a high-energy laser effector to direct concentrated energy towards a target. Its AV_Halo PINPOINT fire-control software maintains precise laser placement on moving targets, including those attempting to manoeuvre during an engagement. AeroVironment says the system integrates AI-enabled detection, tracking and target prioritisation to accelerate engagements against aerial threats.LOCUST X3 features a modular open systems architecture (MOSA), allowing it to integrate different sensors and operate across mobile, fixed, semi-fixed and containerised configurations. The manufacturer also says it can receive targeting information from integrated sensors or higher-level command-and-control systems.Rising drone threat puts Trump's security under greater scrutinyThe deployment comes amid growing concerns over the security threats facing US President Donald Trump, including the potential use of unmanned aerial systems for surveillance or attacks.Small commercial drones are relatively inexpensive, widely accessible and difficult to detect, making them a growing challenge for security agencies protecting high-value individuals and sensitive locations.Trump has faced multiple assassination attempts, including the July 2024 shooting at a campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania. The evolving threat environment has also raised concerns about the use of drones by hostile actors, particularly as advances in autonomous technology and coordinated drone operations make aerial threats more complex.The deployment of laser weapons alongside Avenger missile systems, radar and electronic warfare equipment reflects the US military's growing emphasis on layered counter-drone protection.

articles.title: SEAN PARNELL: The military needs more than recruiting ads — it needs to be seen
articles.summary: Every military branch hit its recruiting mission in fiscal year 2026 under Trump and Secretary Hegseth, with the Army finishing four months early.
articles.body: Three years ago, Washington had written off a generation. Too soft, too unfit, too disconnected to serve. In 2023, the Army, Navy and Air Force all missed their recruiting goals. People in this town started asking out loud whether the all-volunteer force could survive. Some started talking about a draft. They were wrong about the kids. Under President Trump and Secretary Hegseth, every active-duty service met its recruiting mission in fiscal year 2026, and most of them did it months early. The Army signed 61,500 future soldiers with more than four months to spare. The Navy raised its goal by 10% and still hit it in July. It finished the year with 45,112 sailors, three years after coming up 7,450 short of its goal. The Air Force and Space Force had met their goals by April. The Marines said it was the best recruiting environment they'd seen in years, and they already have half of next year's class under contract. RENEWED PATRIOTISM AND CAREER OPPORTUNITIES FUEL ARMY'S BIGGEST RECRUITING SURGE IN YEARS Since November 2024, the military has posted its best rate of recruiting mission achieved in more than 15 years. We did it while American troops were in combat in the Middle East. Across the active-duty force, we saw interest across all demographics, and women’s recruitment is up once again. That strength extended beyond active duty. The Navy Reserve finished at 113% of mission, Marine Corps Reserve at 108%, the Army National Guard at 102%, and the Army Reserve at 103%, its first time surpassing its goal in 10 years. The kids didn't change. The leadership did. President Trump and Secretary Hegseth told young Americans the truth. The military exists to fight and win. The work is hard. Earning your place in it is something to be proud of. It turns out a generation that had been told nothing was worth sacrificing for was hungry to hear that something is. I co-chair the Department of War Recruiting Task Force, and our job is to make sure this year’s success is a starting point, not a high-water mark. Records don't sustain themselves. If we want to keep setting them, I believe we have to do two things. Build propensity, the desire to serve, and create proximity, a military close enough to the American people that the desire turns into a decision. Propensity There's a photo that says this better than I can. A little boy, maybe 5 years old, stands ankle-deep in the surf in a swim shirt, holding up a small American flag. Two Army Apache helicopters are thundering low over the water in front of him. He's never going to forget that day. That's propensity. It comes from moments of awe. Apaches over the surf. Jets ripping over a stadium on a Friday night. A kid climbing into the hatch of a tank at the county fair. No ad campaign can do what those moments do. They make a kid want to be one of us. NAVY SAYS NO REPRIMANDS OR FIRINGS AFTER BLUE ANGELS’ LOW PASS OVER BEACHGOERS That's why this administration has approved more flyovers than any administration before it. The public does the rest. Every flyover is filmed and shared and passed around online, and that sharing costs the taxpayer nothing. We need to build on that with live demonstrations, special operations showcases and Fleet Weeks that don't stop at the coast. There are river towns in the heartland that have never seen a Navy ship. They should. No one grows up wanting to be something they've never seen. Proximity I led an infantry platoon in Afghanistan with the 10th Mountain Division. Every grunt learns the same lesson fast: if you don't hold the ground, you lose it. You can clear a valley in an afternoon. Pull out, and someone else moves in. The only way to hold terrain is to be on it, every day. TRUMP PENTAGON LAUNCHES COMPETITION FOR AMERICA'S NEXT GREAT MILITARY BASE Recruiting is no different. The ground is every town in America, and for 20 years, we've been pulling back from it. We consolidated onto fewer, bigger bases. We left the cities that used to see uniforms every day. Then we acted surprised when young people stopped thinking about serving. What we're left with is a force that's become a family business. We go back to military families again and again because they're the only Americans we still touch on a regular basis. Those families are the backbone of this country, and we owe them more than we can repay. But a force that only recruits from itself is burning through a reserve it can't replace. The Pentagon plans to add 44,000 service members next year. We won't find them unless we reach Americans who have never known anyone in uniform. Proximity is how we take that ground back. We want a recruiting presence in every town in America. Soldiers, sailors, airmen and Marines in dress uniform at the county fair, the Friday night game and the Fourth of July parade, doing the work face to face. New recruits sworn in at halftime. Recruiters who are part of the community, not stuck in a strip-mall office. Guard units out where people can see them. You need both Neither one works alone. Propensity without proximity fades. That boy on the beach is going to need someone in uniform in his hometown when he turns 17. Proximity without propensity is just a recruiting table nobody stops at. Showing up again America's young people never stopped being willing to serve. We just stopped showing up. Under President Trump and Secretary Hegseth, America is back, and so is military service. Now we have to make sure we never stop, in the stadiums, on the beaches, at the fairs and in every town a base will never reach. articles.title: Dia Mirza asks for a cleaner Diwali, BJP sees an 'anti-Hindu' agenda and BMC hits delete: The 'tukde-tukde' jibe, the 'paise nahi liye' retort and a civic body's swift retreat, how the row unfolded
articles.summary: MUMBAI: The Bombay high court on Tuesday expressed its \"deep pain and displeasure\" with the recent row over actor Dia Mirza's video for the BMC's
articles.body: MUMBAI: The Bombay high court on Tuesday expressed its "deep pain and displeasure" with the recent row over actor Dia Mirza's video for the BMC's eco-friendly and firecracker-free Diwali campaign and asked the civic body to re-upload her clip which had earlier been taken down.A bench of Justice Girish Kulkarni and Justice Neela Gokhale, taking suo motu note of the issue, said it was anguished by the "petty mindset" of certain persons, especially those who are representatives of the common man.It was "most unfortunate" that such a colour was given to a video made to spread awareness about the environment and air and noise pollution, the HC bench said.No person can question as to why a certain celebrity was chosen by the authorities to spread awareness, it stated.The controversy erupted after Mumbai BJP chief Ameet Satam objected to Dia Mirza's inclusion in the BMC's eco-friendly Diwali campaign, questioning why the actor was chosen to advise people on celebrating the festival.The 'Tukde-Tukde Gang' jibeFollowing his objection, the civic body removed her video from its social media platforms, while retaining similar campaign clips featuring Madhuri Dixit, Nishigandha Wad and cricketer Ajinkya Rahane, news agency PTI reported.Ameet Satam linked an appeal against the use of firecrackers during Diwali with the "tukde tukde gang", alleging that anti-India forces were attempting to dictate how Hindus should celebrate Diwali.Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde also labelled Mirza "anti-Hindu" and said she would not be included in future BMC programmes or featured on its official platforms.The 'koi paise nahi liye' retortThe actor, meanwhile, responded to the criticism by pointing out that she had made the video in public interest and had not charged the civic body for it. "Koi paise nahi liye hain. Bhalai ka zamana hee nahi raha," she said, according to PTI.Union minister Ramdas Athawale criticised the Rehna Hai Tere Dil Mein actor over the BMC video, advising her to “focus on acting” rather than posting comments against a religion. He said the Constitution gave every religion the right to celebrate its festivals and acknowledged that bursting firecrackers was part of Diwali tradition, while also noting that excessive pollution was a concern.The row drew criticism from opposition leaders, with Mumbai Congress chief Varsha Gaikwad accusing the BJP of politicising an environmental awareness campaign. Union Minister Ramdas Athawale, too, criticised Mirza, saying she should focus on acting rather than religion, ANI reported.What HC saidTaking suo motu cognisance of the controversy, the High Court said the BMC commissioner was right in choosing celebrities to spread awareness and that nobody could question the selection. It also reminded the authorities that its directions against bursting firecrackers on public roads and streets applied throughout the year, irrespective of festivals."Every person, irrespective of their religion and caste, is breathing the same air," the bench observed, stressing that Mumbai's identity rested on togetherness and mutual respect.The court said the BMC's decision to remove the video following political objections was an unwarranted knee-jerk reaction and directed it to restore the clip.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Halloween: Bonfire attack victim has 'serious burns'
articles.summary: Tianna Patterson, 17, witness the boy being attacked before he fell unconscious into the bonfire in Strabane.
articles.body:
The 17-year-old girl who rescued an injured teenage boy from a bonfire said she reacted on instinct.

A local councillor, who spoke to his mother, said he had been left with "severe burns" to his face and hands.

Tianna Patterson said she saw him collapse and fall into the fire and her first thought was to try to help.

She had witnessed him being assaulted only moments earlier.

"I just reached for him by the neck and pulled him out of the bonfire," she said.

"I then got a friend's phone and called the emergency services."

The A Level student at Holy Cross College in Strabane said she had been at the bonfire with friends when the incident happened on Saturday night.

"We are all very proud of her as this could so easily have been a terrible tragedy," she said.

"But thankfully she acted quickly and rescued the young lad and got him help from the emergency services."

Independent councillor Paul Gallagher has spoken to the boy's mother and said she is "distraught".

"Young people have gone to the bonfire and in the chaos of it, a young 17-year-old got knocked unconscious, fell onto a fire which at best can be described as white hot," Gallagher told BBC Radio Foyle's North West Today programme.

"I've spoken to his mother who was very distraught, to say the least."

Gallagher said the boy will now require extensive medical care and it will take a long time for him to recover.

"The chaos around a bonfire is madness and it should never have happened that a young boy gets knocked out and put on a fire.

"Bonfires bring very little benefit, they are destructive, they are a serious danger to young people."

The police are stepping up their hunt for the boy's attacker but no arrests have been made.

They have appealed for witnesses to come forward, including anyone who may have captured the attack on their mobile phones.
